peripatus.name: Peripatus
peripatus.description: A primitive, caterpillar-like terrestrial invertebrate known as a "living fossil."

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)
features.Respiratory type: Tracheal system (Tracheae open through diffused spiracles)

sizeStructure: Size: Small body ranging from 2 cm to 15 cm in length.
Shape: Worm-like, cylindrical, and caterpillar-like body with unjointed legs (lobopods).
Colour: Dark grey, brown, or reddish, matching the soil or leaf litter.
Special external features: Skin has a velvety texture due to numerous minute papillae; head bears a pair of antennae and oral papillae.
ecology: Acts as a predator, feeding on small invertebrates like termites, beetles, and snails.
Serves as a prey for larger predators such as birds, lizards, and spiders.
Functions as an indicator of a healthy, moist forest ecosystem.
economy: Scientific Importance: Vital evolutionary evidence as a connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.
Research: Studied for its unique projectile slime mechanism (bio-adhesives).
Biodiversity: Represents an ancient lineage unchanged for millions of years (Living Fossil).

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

sizeStructure: Size: Varies by species, generally elongated, ranging from 2.5 cm to over 30 cm (e.g., P. malcolmsonii).
Shape: Spindle-shaped, bilaterally symmetrical body divided into cephalothorax and abdomen.
Colour: Usually pale blue or translucent white, turning orange-red when cooked.
Special external features: Body protected by a hard carapace with a serrated, saw-like rostrum extending forward; possesses 19 pairs of jointed appendages.
ecology: Acts as a scavenger and omnivore, feeding on algae, decaying matter, and small insects.
Serves as a primary food source for larger aquatic predators like fish and water birds.
Helps in cleaning the water body by consuming organic debris and detritus.
economy: Food Industry: A major source of protein, widely consumed globally as a delicacy.
Aquaculture: Extensively farmed in "Prawn Culture" industries due to high growth rates.
Economy: High commercial export value contributes significantly to the fisheries economy.

introduction: It inhabits freshwater rivers, lakes, and canals, though larvae often require brackish water. It is nocturnal, bottom-dwelling, and highly aggressive, known for its massive growth potential in aquaculture.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

sizeStructure: Size: Large-bodied, reaching 30 cm or more in species like M. rosenbergii.
Shape: Elongated, cylindrical body with a rigid cephalothorax and muscular abdomen.
Colour: Greenish-blue to brownish-grey; mature males often have deep blue claws.
Special external features: Characterized by extremely long, powerful second pair of walking legs (chelipeds) and a long, serrated rostrum.
ecology: Dominant benthic predator and scavenger in freshwater ecosystems.
Controls populations of snails and aquatic insects.
Serves as a key food source for predatory fish, wetland birds, and otters.
economy: Aquaculture: The primary species for freshwater prawn farming (Blue Revolution).
Food Industry: High-value export product marketed globally as Scampi.
Livelihood: Provides significant income for inland fish farmers in tropical regions.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

australopithecus_robustus.name: Australopithecus robustus
australopithecus_robustus.description: Australopithecus robustus had strong skull features. Specialized for heavy plant chewing. Part of side branch of human evolution.
introduction: Did not directly lead to modern humans.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

homo_habilis.name: Homo habilis
homo_habilis.description: Homo habilis was an early human species. It is known for making simple stone tools. Shows increase in brain size compared to Australopithecus.
introduction: Homo habilis lived about 2.4–1.4 million years ago.
Fossils were found in East Africa.
It marks the beginning of the genus Homo.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

homo_erectus.name: Homo erectus
homo_erectus.description: Homo erectus showed fully upright posture. It used advanced stone tools. First hominin to migrate out of Africa.
introduction: Homo erectus lived about 1.9 million–140,000 years ago.
Fossils found in Africa and Asia.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

homo_neanderthalensis.name: Homo neanderthalensis
homo_neanderthalensis.description: Homo neanderthalensis was a close relative of modern humans. Adapted to cold climates. Had large brain capacity.
introduction: Fossils found in Europe and Western Asia.
They coexisted with early Homo sapiens.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

homo_sapiens.name: Homo sapiens
homo_sapiens.description: Highly intelligent primate. Upright posture. Complex language ability.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

cephalaspis.name: Cephalaspis ✝︎
cephalaspis.description: Cephalaspis was a jawless armored fish. Belonged to Ostracodermi. Had bony head shield.
introduction: Fossils found in Europe and North America.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

climatius.name: Climatius ✝︎
climatius.description: Climatius was an early jawed fish. Belonged to Acanthodii group. Had multiple fin spines.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

hylonomus.name: Hylonomus ✝︎
hylonomus.description: Hylonomus is one of the earliest known reptiles. It lived during the Carboniferous period. Shows early adaptation to terrestrial life.
introduction: Hylonomus lived about 315 million years ago.
Fossils were found in North America.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

diomedea.name: Diomedea
diomedea.description: Albatross is a large seabird. Has very long wings. Excellent glider.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

raphus_cucullatus.name: Raphus cucullatus ✝︎
raphus_cucullatus.description: Raphus cucullatus was a flightless bird. Endemic to Mauritius. Extinct due to human activity.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)

hydra.name: Hydra
hydra.description: Hydra is a small freshwater cnidarian. It is solitary and attached. Used widely in regeneration studies.
introduction: Hydra lives in freshwater ponds and streams.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

obelia.name: Obelia
obelia.description: Obelia is a marine colonial hydrozoan. Shows alternation of generations.
introduction: Obelia lives attached to rocks in seas.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

physalia.name: Physalia
physalia.description: Physalia is a floating colonial hydrozoan. Highly poisonous tentacles present.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

aurelia.name: Aurelia
aurelia.description: Aurelia is a free-swimming jellyfish. Medusa stage dominant.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan
features.Nervous system: Nerve net with marginal sense organs

adamsia.name: Adamsia
adamsia.description: Adamsia is a marine sea anemone. Shows commensalism with hermit crab.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

pennatula.name: Pennatula
pennatula.description: Pennatula is a colonial marine cnidarian. It lives partially embedded in soft sea floor. Known for feather-like appearance.
introduction: Plays a role in benthic ecosystems.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

gorgonia.name: Gorgonia
gorgonia.description: Gorgonia is a colonial soft coral. It forms fan-shaped branching colonies. Common in coral reefs.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

meandrina.name: Meandrina
meandrina.description: Meandrina is a massive stony coral. It forms brain-like colonies. Important reef builder.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

metridium.name: Metridium
metridium.description: Metridium is a large sea anemone. It is solitary and sessile. Found in cold marine waters.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

corallium.name: Corallium
corallium.description: Corallium is a precious coral genus. Produces red calcareous skeleton. Used in jewellery.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

antipatharia.name: Antipatharia
antipatharia.description: Antipatharia includes black corals. They form branching colonies. Known for dark spiny skeleton.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

ctenoplana.name: Ctenoplana
ctenoplana.description: Ctenoplana is a benthic ctenophore. It creeps on sea bottom surfaces. Represents primitive ctenophores.
introduction: Ctenoplana lives in shallow marine waters.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

pleurobrachia.name: Pleurobrachia
pleurobrachia.description: Pleurobrachia is a free-swimming ctenophore. Body is spherical with long tentacles. Commonly studied comb jelly.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

hormiphora.name: Hormiphora
hormiphora.description: Hormiphora is a cydippid ctenophore. Closely resembles Pleurobrachia. Pelagic and transparent.
introduction: Hormiphora lives in open marine waters.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

cestum.name: Cestum
cestum.description: Cestum is a ribbon-like ctenophore. Largest known comb jelly. Highly elongated body.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

beroe.name: Beroe
beroe.description: Beroe is a tentacleless ctenophore. Active predator of other ctenophores. Highly muscular body.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

asterias.name: Asterias
asterias.description:
Asterias is a typical starfish.
It has five arms and a central disc.
It represents Class Asteroidea.
introduction: Asterias lives in shallow marine waters.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan, Deuterostomous

astropecten.name: Astropecten
astropecten.description:
Astropecten is a fast-moving starfish.
It lives on sandy sea floors.
Adapted for burrowing life.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan, Deuterostomous

pentaceros.name: Pentaceros
pentaceros.description:
Pentaceros is a large starfish.
It has strong horn-like spines.
Body is heavily armoured.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan, Deuterostomous

ophiothrix.name: Ophiothrix
ophiothrix.description:
Ophiothrix has long flexible arms.
Body is delicate and fast-moving.
Belongs to Class Ophiuroidea.
introduction: Ophiothrix lives under rocks and corals.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan, Deuterostomous

ophiura.name: Ophiura
ophiura.description:
Ophiura has a distinct central disc.
Arms are long and whip-like.
Moves rapidly using arms.
introduction: Ophiura lives on muddy sea bottoms.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan, Deuterostomous

echinus.name: Echinus
echinus.description:
Echinus is a globular echinoderm.
Body is covered with movable spines.
Common in marine habitats.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan

echinocardium.name: Echinocardium
echinocardium.description:
Echinocardium has a heart-shaped body.
Adapted for burrowing life.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan

cucumaria.name: Cucumaria
cucumaria.description:
Cucumaria has elongated body.
Body wall is leathery.
Tentacles present around mouth.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan

holothuria.name: Holothuria
holothuria.description:
Holothuria has elongated soft body.
Lacks arms and spines.
introduction: Holothuria lives on sandy sea floor.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan

antedon.name: Antedon
antedon.description:
Antedon is a free-swimming crinoid.
Has feather-like arms.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan

balanoglossus.name: Balanoglossus
balanoglossus.description:
Balanoglossus is a marine, worm-like animal.
It lives buried in sand or mud.
It shows features linking invertebrates and chordates.
introduction: Balanoglossus is a free-living marine hemichordate.
It inhabits sandy and muddy sea shores.
It is important in understanding chordate evolution.

sizeStructure: Body divided into proboscis, collar, and trunk
Numerous gill slits in trunk region
ecology: Helps nutrient recycling in coastal areas

saccoglossus.name: Saccoglossus
saccoglossus.description:
Saccoglossus is a small marine acorn worm.
It lives in U-shaped burrows.
It shows basic chordate-like features.
introduction: It inhabits sandy and muddy coastal regions.
It is important in evolutionary studies.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)
features.Nervous system: Diffuse nerve net with dorsal nerve cord

ptychodera-flava.name: Ptychodera flava
ptychodera-flava.description:
Ptychodera flava is a large acorn worm.
It lives buried in marine sediments.
It clearly shows hemichordate characters.
introduction: Ptychodera flava is a free-living marine animal.
It inhabits shallow sandy and muddy shores.
It is important for studying chordate ancestry.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Deuterostomous)
features.Nervous system: Diffuse nerve net with dorsal nerve cord

ecology: Part of coastal benthic food web
economy: Helps understand origin of chordate traits

chaetopleura.name: Chaetopleura
chaetopleura.description: Chaetopleura is a marine mollusc with a flattened body. It has eight shell plates on the dorsal side. It lives attached to rocks.
introduction: Chaetopleura is a benthic marine mollusc found on rocky shores.
It moves slowly and grazes on algae.
It helps maintain algal balance in coastal habitats.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

chiton.name: Chiton
chiton.description: Chiton is a marine mollusc with segmented shell plates. It firmly clings to rocks. It is a slow-moving grazer.
introduction: Chiton lives on rocky sea shores.
It feeds on algae scraped from surfaces.
It is common in intertidal zones.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

dentalium.name: Dentalium
dentalium.description: Dentalium has a long tubular shell. It lives buried in sand. It is a marine burrowing mollusc.
introduction: Dentalium inhabits sandy and muddy sea floors.
It is important in benthic ecosystems.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

pila_globosa.name: Pila globosa
pila_globosa.description: Pila globosa is a freshwater snail. It has a globular shell. It is amphibious in habit.
introduction: Pila globosa lives in ponds and slow rivers.
It is important in freshwater ecosystems.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

aplysia.name: Aplysia
aplysia.description: Aplysia is a soft-bodied marine gastropod. It is large and slow-moving. Known for neurobiology studies.
introduction: It is important in nervous system research.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

conus_marmoreus.name: Conus marmoreus
conus_marmoreus.description: Conus marmoreus is a venomous snail. It uses a harpoon-like radula. Found in coral reefs.
introduction: Conus marmoreus lives in tropical seas.
It is important in toxin research.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

unio.name: Unio
unio.description: Unio is a freshwater bivalve mollusc. Body is laterally compressed. Shell is heavy and thick.
introduction: Unio lives buried in river and pond beds.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

mytilus.name: Mytilus
mytilus.description: Mytilus is a marine bivalve. It attaches to rocks by byssus threads. Shell is elongated.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

lamellidens.name: Lamellidens
lamellidens.description: Lamellidens is a freshwater bivalve. Shell is large and thick. Known for pearl formation.
introduction: Lamellidens lives in ponds and rivers.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

pinctada.name: Pinctada
pinctada.description: Pinctada is a marine bivalve. Produces natural pearls. Shell is smooth and shiny.
introduction: Pinctada lives attached to rocks in seas.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

spondylus.name: Spondylus
spondylus.description: Spondylus has spiny shells. It is a marine bivalve. Shells are brightly coloured.
introduction: Spondylus lives attached to hard substrates.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

ostrea.name: Ostrea
ostrea.description: Ostrea is a marine bivalve. Shells are irregular and rough. Sessile filter feeder.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

loligo.name: Loligo
loligo.description: Loligo is a fast-swimming cephalopod. It has ten arms. Ink sac present.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

nautilus.name: Nautilus
nautilus.description: Nautilus is a living fossil. Shell is coiled and chambered. Primitive cephalopod.
introduction: Nautilus lives in deep marine waters.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

octopus.name: Octopus
octopus.description: Octopus has eight arms. Highly intelligent mollusc. Shell absent.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

sepia.name: Sepia
sepia.description: Sepia has an internal cuttlebone. Body is flattened. Excellent camouflage ability.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

architeuthes.name: Architeuthes
architeuthes.description: Architeuthes is the largest invertebrate. Lives in deep oceans. Rarely seen alive.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

neopilina_galathea.name: Neopilina galathea
neopilina_galathea.description: Neopilina galathea is a primitive mollusc. Shell is single and cap-like. Shows segmentation.

features.Body plan: Tube within a tube body plan (Protostomous)

dugesia.name: Dugesia
dugesia.description: Dugesia is a free-living flatworm. It is well known for regeneration ability. Commonly found in freshwater habitats.
introduction: Dugesia lives in freshwater ponds and streams.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

fasciola.name: Fasciola hepatica
fasciola.description: Fasciola hepatica is a parasitic flatworm. It infects liver of sheep and cattle. Causes fascioliasis.
introduction: Fasciola hepatica lives as an endoparasite.
It requires snail as intermediate host.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

schistosoma.name: Schistosoma
schistosoma.description: Schistosoma is a parasitic flatworm. Sexes are separate. Causes schistosomiasis.
introduction: Schistosoma inhabits blood vessels of humans.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

taenia-solium.name: Taenia solium
taenia-solium.description: Taenia solium is a parasitic tapeworm. Human is definitive host. Causes taeniasis and cysticercosis.
introduction: Taenia solium lives in human intestine.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

taenia-saginata.name: Taenia saginata
taenia-saginata.description: Taenia saginata is a parasitic tapeworm. Humans are definitive hosts. Does not cause cysticercosis.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

echinococcus.name: Echinococcus
echinococcus.description: Echinococcus is a small parasitic tapeworm. Causes hydatid disease. Highly dangerous to humans.
introduction: Echinococcus lives in intestine of dogs.

features.Body plan: Blind sac body plan

sycon.name: Sycon
sycon.description: Sycon is a simple marine sponge. It shows syconoid canal system. Commonly used as a poriferan example.
introduction: Sycon lives in shallow marine waters.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

leucosolenia.name: Leucosolenia
leucosolenia.description: Leucosolenia is a primitive sponge. It shows asconoid canal system. Marine and colonial.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

grantia.name: Grantia
grantia.description: Grantia is a syconoid sponge. Body wall is folded. Marine and solitary.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

euplectella.name: Euplectella
euplectella.description: Euplectella is a deep-sea glass sponge. Skeleton is siliceous. Shows beautiful lattice structure.
introduction: Euplectella lives in deep marine waters.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

hyalonema.name: Hyalonema
hyalonema.description: Hyalonema is a deep-sea sponge. It has long twisted spicules. Belongs to glass sponges.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

spongilla.name: Spongilla
spongilla.description: Spongilla is a freshwater sponge. Forms gemmules. Common in ponds and lakes.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

euspongia.name: Euspongia
euspongia.description: Euspongia is a commercial sponge. Skeleton is spongin fibers. Used as natural sponge.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

cliona.name: Cliona
cliona.description: Cliona is a coral-boring sponge. It bores into shells and corals. Causes bioerosion.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

xestospongia.name: Xestospongia
xestospongia.description: Xestospongia is a large marine sponge. Also called redwood of the reef. Very long-lived sponge.

features.Body plan: Cell aggregate body plan

chalina.name: Chalina
chalina.description: Chalina is a branching marine sponge. Soft and flexible body. Common on coral reefs.
introduction: Chalina lives in shallow marine waters.
